summary.headline: Gala Precision FY26 revenue rose 32% to INR314 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.51% on a ~1% (INR3.23 crore) forex loss.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was about INR95 crores (up 26% YoY), with EBITDA of about INR17 crores (up 31%, margin 17.57%) and net profit of about INR12 crores (up 22%, PAT margin 12.9%). For FY26, revenue reached INR314 crores (up 32%), EBITDA INR52 crores (up 27%, margin 16.51%), and profit after exceptional items INR36 crores (up 32%). Management attributed the annual margin dip mainly to a forex loss, and said raw material costs are passed through to customers with a lag. The Chennai fastener plant reached a Phase 1 run-rate of about INR5 crores per month, with Phase 2 expected to add capacity by mid-2026.

segments.name: DSS (disc spring)
segments.commentary: Largest segment at about 49% of FY26 revenue, described as a stable recurring base.

segments.name: SFS (special fastening solutions)
segments.commentary: Crossed INR100 crores, reaching INR108 crores in FY26 (+64% YoY); about 34% of revenue and fastest growing, with fasteners sales of about INR100 crores.

segments.name: CSS (coil spring)
segments.commentary: About 17% of FY26 revenue, supported by steady industrial and mobility demand.

guidance_outlook: Company growth target of 20% to 25% in overall revenue; wind segment fasteners and springs targeted at 25% to 30% in the short term.
Chennai FY27 sales expected at about INR80 crores (67% to 70% of INR120 crores capacity); capacity to reach INR10 crores per month by end of FY27.
Cash flow guidance: maintain or improve cash-flow conversion by about 10% YoY; inventory days at 103, with a target to cut about 10 days.
EBITDA margin expected to stabilise in the 17% to 19% range by FY27 end, assuming no further forex volatility.
Export share expected to stay at 35% to 40% of sales.
Offshore wind expected to contribute about 10% of fastener sales within two to three years.
EU-India FTA expected to take effect around January 2027, removing the 3.7% EU import duty, though CBAM may offset the benefit.
Wada land (5 to 10 acres) expected to be finalised around June-end or July 2026; new plant build of 15 to 18 months; FY27 capex about INR50 crores, funded by internal accruals and bank borrowings.
capex_capacity: Chennai fastener plant: installed capacity 4,600 MT; Phase 1 reached about INR5 crores per month (about INR60 crores annualised) from August 2025 ramp-up; plant utilisation about 35% in FY26.
Chennai Phase 2 capex to complete by June-July 2026, adding another INR5 crores per month (about INR60 crores annual); total Chennai capacity INR120 crores per annum by year-end.
Wada plant: no additional land; disc spring running about 80% utilisation; coil spring and fastener capacity have headroom, to be unlocked via productivity, line balancing and outsourcing.
Wada land purchase of 5 to 10 acres under negotiation for an own-land expansion; Chennai backup option is a SIPCOT long lease or an existing building to shift stud manufacturing.
Renewable and mobility capex: 1.8 MW open access solar plant ordered for captive consumption.
demand_pricing: Wind: about 60% to 65% of wind sales from India and 30% to 35% from exports; first high-tensile bolt supply to a global wind OEM in India from Chennai in Q4 FY26.
Growth mix in FY26 cited as about 10% from new customers, 10% to 12% from new parts with existing customers, and 5% to 7% organic growth.
Addressable market expanded: studs cover about US$1 billion; bolts and nuts take it to about US$2.5 billion. Global fastener market cited at about US$100 billion.
CSS competitors named as NHK Spring and Stumpp Schuele & Somappa; some imports from Europe remain a substitution opportunity.
Raw materials are 100% passed through to customers; process costs (gas, diesel) are being repriced from April 2026, with recovery expected on an annualised basis.
Hedging policy cut from 70% to 40% of estimated export collections, covering 12 months, net of imports for USD exposure.
Management says a currency depreciation gave a top-line benefit in Q4 but also created a non-cash forward-cover loss; the amount was not quantified on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What wind-energy order book and growth visibility exist for the coming year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 25% to 30% growth in short-term wind fasteners and springs; wind sales are about 60% to 65% India and 30% to 35% exports.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Chennai revenue ramp and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 ramped from INR1 crore to INR5 crores per month from August; Phase 2 adds INR5 crores per month by June-July, with INR80 crores targeted for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall to 16.5%, and how is raw-material inflation handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the drop from about 17.1% mainly to a roughly 1% (INR3.23 crore) forex loss, not mix or raw materials; raw materials are fully passed through with a lag.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a land and expansion plan beyond Chennai?
qa_highlights.answer: Wada land (2 to 3 plots) is in advanced talks, likely finalised June-end or July; a 15 to 18 month build is expected, with about INR50 crores of capex in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the EU-India FTA and CBAM matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Current EU import duty of 3.7% on Gala products would fall to zero when the FTA takes effect around January 2027, but CBAM could offset the benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedging policy and export mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Forward cover is set at up to 40% of estimated export collections for 12 months; exports are expected to remain 35% to 40% of sales.

risks_watch: Forex volatility: a forex loss of about INR3.23 crores hit FY26 margins, and forward-cover losses can distort quarterly profit.
Chennai utilisation: FY26 was about 35%; the FY27 target of about INR80 crores depends on Phase 2 commissioning by mid-2026 and on scaling the bolt business.
Inventory: Chennai ramp-up adds inventory; working-capital days (103) and cash conversion are a watch item.
Wada land acquisition timelines could slip; Chennai backup plan depends on a SIPCOT lease or an existing building.
Pending patent suit on wedge lock washers: next hearing in June 2026; no arguments yet.
CBAM and EU trade changes could offset the expected FTA duty benefit.
Raw-material and gas cost pass-through is lagged; quarterly margin volatility is possible before price revisions take effect.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and capacity plans, with specific timelines. Cautious and hedged on land acquisition and on quarterly forex and cost pass-through effects. Several answers were loosely worded, and exact figures (such as the currency benefit to revenue) were deferred.

On the annualized basis, we will definitely see that whatever is been incurred is recovered.
